Executive summary

Stable value, very different composition

1

2025 was a strong year for the core business

IAS (Ltd + Côte d'Ivoire branch) grew audited turnover by 16% to €17.65M and gross operating surplus (EBE) by 39% to €6.74M, a 38.2% margin. Net income fell 21% to €3.04M because the H145 lease added a full year of depreciation and interest, and FX losses rose. The August-2025 forecast for IAS was within 2% on turnover and EBITDA.

2

Group valuation , on August 2025

Same method (40% DCF, 40% EBITDA multiple, 20% revenue multiple) and parameters. The DCF falls by because the IAS 5-year cash-flow forecast is flat after 2026 (2030 IAS turnover vs a year ago); the multiples add because they now start from a stronger 2026 (base year rolled forward).

3

Value rests on assumptions to validate

of the value comes from the 2025-to-2026 IAS step-up (largely HID ACMI leases), and of 2026 group turnover is Max'Air and FAS, which have no 2025 accounts. ENI Côte d'Ivoire is only contracted to September 2027.

4

The method leaves out debt, tax and capex

Adjusted net debt is (H145 lease, provisions and the off-balance-sheet N3 leases, less cash) and IAS books no income tax (a 25% tax would cost about of DCF value). On these adjustments the indicative value is ; the v2 FCFF model gives €40.7M.

5

Assets and contracts support the collateral case

Fleet value after the July-2026 technical appraisal (at least €6.8M above book value); contract book (present value of probability-weighted revenue). Cash collection (about 246 days of sales) is the main operating weakness.

    01 · Our founder and history

    Our Founder and History

    Four decades growing alongside West Africa

    The group was founded in the late 1970s in Côte d'Ivoire to support the country's agricultural expansion. Mr. Hugues Moreau is its single owner and legal representative.

    The business then grew alongside commodity extraction and trading, serving the agricultural, oil and gas (onshore and offshore) and mining sectors, and later added personal transportation and medical evacuation.

    IAS was the first private aviation company in West Africa and remains uniquely positioned in the region; Ivoire Hélicoptère has operated in Côte d'Ivoire since 1981. In difficult years and periods of political crisis the business kept expanding, because turmoil raised demand for secure and emergency transport of people and goods.

    The group now has companies in Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana and Burkina Faso holding 5 air operator certificates. Guinea has been added in 2026, and an operation in Senegal is being prepared.

    03 · Market opportunities

    Market Opportunities

    Offshore gas, gold and security keep demand structurally high Updated

    Oil & Gas

    ENI's Baleine and Calao discoveries since 2021 opened up the Ivorian offshore, with reserves of about 2 billion barrels. IAS has served ENI since exploration began and holds an extension to September 2027. Murphy and other US operators are preparing campaigns (Murphy: 1-year exploration contract from 2027). In Ghana, ENI is expected to tender a 3+2-year contract. In Senegal, Woodside (Sangomar) and BP are served by a single foreign operator under a sharing agreement; a Woodside tender drew over ten expressions of interest, including IAS with Dakar Offshore.

    Gold & mining

    High gold prices sustain exploration and production in Ghana, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. Bullion transport is contracted through Brinks, whose relationship with IAS goes back about 20 years. Guinea is seen as the next mining frontier: GAS targets mine-site crew transport, light precious-metals transport and medevac, where poor roads make air transport essential.

    Security, humanitarian & institutions

    Volatile security keeps private air transport a priority in crises for private and institutional clients alike. In Burkina Faso, FAS is expanding humanitarian missions, and medical services and power companies are served in every country.

    Market tension. Aircraft and qualified crew are scarce worldwide. New H145 deliveries are quoted around 2030, and a 2–4-year-old pre-owned H145 now costs about €12.5M, against roughly €10M paid for IAS's current H145 (meeting, 6-Oct-2026).

    06 · Our local companies and operator certificates

    Local Companies & Operator Certificates

    Five operating companies, plus Guinea in approval Updated
    IAS · Rotary-wing AOC, Côte d'Ivoire

    Offshore helicopter transport since 2002 at IOGP standard. Long-standing partner of Petroci; serves every producing O&G company offshore Côte d'Ivoire. Partner of the Baleine and Calao discoveries. Sole Airbus maintenance centre for the region since 2014. 2025: €17.65M turnover, 96 staff.

    Ivoire Hélicoptère
    IH · Aerial work & onshore, Côte d'Ivoire

    Operating since 1981, the first company of its kind in the region. Crop spraying, power-line surveys, passenger and VIP flights, medevac, bullion transport and geophysical surveys. Preferred partner of local authorities and institutions.

    MAXAIR · Fixed-wing AOC, Côte d'Ivoire

    Since 2012: passenger, VIP, emergency and medevac flights and precious metals; the only company of its kind in CIV, operating Beech 200s. Capital raised to FCFA 872M, 98.62% held by IAS Ltd. 2025 accounts not provided

    GHSL · Ghana

    Gold Helicopter Services: passenger, VIP, medevac, onshore and offshore flights out of Accra; present in Ghana since the late 1980s. Member of the Petroleum Commission, with a key role in discoveries such as Jubilee. Its activity (Brinks Ghana, Ghana staff) appears in the IAS forecast.

    FAS · Burkina Faso

    Humanitarian, passenger, VIP, medevac and emergency flights out of Ouagadougou since 2019. Lessor (under its AOC) of the Dauphin leased to GAS on ACMI terms. 2025 accounts not provided

    GAS New
    Guinée Aircraft Services · Guinea

    Incorporated 2026 in Conakry (RCCM GN.TCC.2026.B.08507), GNF 150M capital, 100% H. Moreau. AOC application filed 30-Sep-2026. Accountable manager E. Boutros; 2 Dauphin N3. See Expansion.

    Revenue by scenario · group, € M

    ContractedRisk-weightedManagement

    ENI Côte d'Ivoire: defend, on the right terms

    The new terms (USD 546k/month standing charge with 2 H145s) barely pay for a second, €12.5M aircraft, which leaves the renewal roughly value-neutral. Winning it while serving it with the existing H145 and Dauphin backup would add about €3.3M. Negotiating the fleet requirement is worth as much as the tender itself.

    ENI Ghana & Murphy: pursue

    ENI Ghana gives the best equity IRR with ECA debt (35%). Murphy uses existing Dauphins, so it needs no capex and is pure upside.

    Woodside Senegal: be selective

    Two new H145s, a new AOC and partner set-up, more than 10 bidders and political pressure. On current assumptions the equity IRR is -9%. Bid only with lease-backed aircraft or better pricing.

    Capacity constraint. Alexandra Rotaru: "we can't win all the tenders at the same time". The management case, in which every tender is won, needs 4 H145s plus crews in 2027 and is a ceiling, not a forecast.

    16 · Fleet financing & funding options New

    Fleet Financing: Debt, Equity or Lease

    Meeting action item: compare funding alternatives for up to four H145 D3
    Figures in this chapter come from the business-plan (FCFF, v2) analysis; the group valuation is in the Valuation Model chapter.

    A. ECA-backed debt

    −€8.8M

    7-year NPV cost per aircraft, incl. mismatch risk

    Euler Hermes cover with a bank (Apple Bank on the first deal): 85% LTV, about 5.7%, 7 years. A proven route, the asset stays owned, and upfront cash is −€2.4M per aircraft.

    B. New equity

    55%

    dilution of the owner for the full programme

    No debt service or rent, but at the current value it means giving up 55% for 4 aircraft. Investors would expect about 20% a year. Management sees it as a fallback option.

    C. Operating lease

    −€9.2M

    7-year NPV cost per aircraft, incl. mismatch risk

    No upfront cash, which protects treasury during the Guinea start-up. But lessors want 5+1+1 years against 3-year client contracts, a mismatch of −€1.1M per aircraft.

    Debt capacity: full programme on ECA debt

    Management-case EBITDA ÷ (existing lease service + new annuities). Lenders usually want 1.2–1.3x or more.

    Recommendation

    1

    Anchor contracts → ECA debt

    Finance aircraft for long, high-probability contracts (ENI CI renewal, ENI Ghana) through Euler Hermes-backed loans, building on the performing first deal. Lower cost: ECA-backed debt (Euler Hermes + bank).

    2

    Speculative markets → leases

    Use operating leases (H160 proposal pending) for Senegal-type wins only where redeployment to Ghana or CIV is credible. Push clients for 3+1+1 terms with early commitment.

    3

    Keep equity as a fallback

    Raise equity only if leverage or treasury limits bind, ideally at holding level after the 2025 accounts of all subsidiaries are available.
